title: ISSN Position Stand: Safety and Efficacy of Creatine Supplementation in Exercise, Sport, and Medicine (Kreider et al. 2017)
content: Kreider RB et al., Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition 2017 — Creatine monohydrate is one of the most extensively researched and effective ergogenic nutritional supplements available to athletes, with a strong safety record in healthy individuals at recommended doses. Common protocols: a maintenance dose of ~3-5 g/day (loading phase of ~20g/day for 5-7 days is optional and only speeds up saturation, not required for eventual benefit).

title: ISSN Position Stand: Safety and Efficacy of Creatine Supplementation in Exercise, Sport, and Medicine (Kreider et al. 2017)
content: ISSN Creatine 2017 — Creatine supplementation, combined with resistance training, can increase strength, power, and lean body mass more than training alone for many healthy adults. Product implication: creatine can be presented as an evidence-supported OPTIONAL addition for healthy adults with an appropriate goal — never as a required part of a base meal plan, and never auto-added without the user opting in (Part 8's 'food first, supplements are optional' rule).
